+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static homepage with a browser-only encrypted delivery notebook. Build the committed browser bundle after changing `src/`:
+
+```sh
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm build
+pnpm test
+```
+
+Serve the repository as static files over HTTPS. The existing `start` script is unchanged. No server or browser verification was performed for this change.
+
+## Encryption and storage
+
+`src/encryption.js` uses the pinned [noble-post-quantum hybrid KEM](https://github.com/paulmillr/noble-post-quantum#hybrid-x-wing-kitchensink-and-others) (X-Wing / ML-KEM-768 + X25519). This bundled implementation retains hybrid protection in browsers without experimental native KEM support; there is no silent classical downgrade. Each note gets a fresh encapsulation, 32-byte HKDF salt and 12-byte AES-GCM IV. HKDF-SHA-256 derives a non-extractable AES-256 key with a protocol-specific record context. AES-GCM uses a 128-bit authentication tag and authenticates the version, suite, record ID and creation time. The encrypted envelope includes everything needed for decapsulation and decryption except the recipient private key.
+
+`src/storage.js` initializes a per-browser recipient once, including across concurrent tabs. Its private key is encrypted with a non-extractable WebCrypto AES-GCM key before persistence. That wrapping CryptoKey, the wrapped private key, public key and encrypted note are stored in IndexedDB. Shared secrets and temporary private-key byte buffers are overwritten after use, subject to JavaScript runtime memory-management limitations. No plaintext notes enter localStorage, URLs, network requests or logs. Revealed notes automatically hide after 30 seconds; tab visibility changes clear both the reveal and draft. Storage or crypto failures fail closed and never fall back to plaintext submission.
+
+This is explicitly **local storage**, not end-to-end delivery to staff: there is no order API or authenticated delivery-team public key in this repository. Anyone able to use this browser profile can reveal notes, and same-origin malicious JavaScript can access the vault. Clearing site data permanently removes both notes and their keys. Delete removes the current note record and draft, but does not promise forensic erasure from browser storage or backups. The library is not independently audited; see its upstream security documentation.
+
+For an actual order integration, provision an authenticated delivery-team public key, encrypt to that key, and send only the envelope with an authorized order identifier over HTTPS. Keep the team's private key outside the customer browser; provide authenticated recipient-side decryption and server authorization and retention controls. Local browser keys must not be mistaken for delivery-team identity.
+
+## Checks
+
+Node tests cover hybrid encryption/decryption, Unicode, fresh per-save randomness, size validation, and authentication failures for altered ciphertext, capsule, IV, salt, record metadata and wrong recipient keys. The static browser bundle is built with esbuild; no CDN JavaScript is loaded at runtime.

+import { ml_kem768_x25519 as kem } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+
+export const SUITE = 'X-Wing+HKDF-SHA256+AES-256-GCM';
+const encode = (value) => new TextEncoder().encode(value);
+export const createRecipient = () => kem.keygen();
+const aad = (record) => encode(JSON.stringify([record.version, record.suite, record.id, record.createdAt]));
+
+async function deriveKey(secret, salt, context) {
+  try {
+    const base = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+    return await crypto.subtle.deriveKey(
+      { name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt, info: context },
+      base, { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt'],
+    );
+  } finally { secret.fill(0); }
+}
+
+export async function encryptNote(publicKey, text) {
+  if (!text.trim() || text.length > 1000) throw new Error('Invalid note length');
+  const record = {
+    version: 1, suite: SUITE, id: crypto.randomUUID(), createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
+    iv: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12)),
+    salt: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)),
+  };
+  const { cipherText, sharedSecret } = kem.encapsulate(publicKey);
+  record.capsule = cipherText;
+  const context = aad(record);
+  const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, record.salt, encode(`daily-grind/delivery-note/v1:${record.id}`));
+  const plaintext = encode(text);
+  try {
+    record.ciphertext = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.encrypt(
+      { name: 'AES-GCM', iv: record.iv, additionalData: context, tagLength: 128 }, key, plaintext,
+    ));
+    return record;
+  } finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+}
+
+export async function decryptNote(secretKey, record) {
+  if (record.version !== 1 || record.suite !== SUITE || typeof record.id !== 'string' ||
+      typeof record.createdAt !== 'string' || record.iv?.length !== 12 || record.salt?.length !== 32 ||
+      record.capsule?.length !== kem.lengths.cipherText || record.ciphertext?.length < 16 ||
+      record.ciphertext?.length > 4016) throw new Error('Invalid encrypted note');
+  const sharedSecret = kem.decapsulate(record.capsule, secretKey);
+  const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, record.salt, encode(`daily-grind/delivery-note/v1:${record.id}`));
+  const bytes = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt(
+    { name: 'AES-GCM', iv: record.iv, additionalData: aad(record), tagLength: 128 }, key, record.ciphertext,
+  ));
+  try { return new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(bytes); }
+  finally { bytes.fill(0); }
+}

+import { createRecipient } from './encryption.js';
+
+export function openVault() {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const request = indexedDB.open('daily-grind-private-notes', 1);
+    request.onupgradeneeded = () => request.result.createObjectStore('vault');
+    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
+    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
+    request.onblocked = () => reject(new Error('Storage blocked'));
+  });
+}
+export function read(db, key) {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const tx = db.transaction('vault', 'readonly');
+    const request = tx.objectStore('vault').get(key);
+    tx.oncomplete = () => resolve(request.result);
+    tx.onerror = tx.onabort = () => reject(tx.error);
+  });
+}
+export function write(db, key, value) {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const tx = db.transaction('vault', 'readwrite');
+    if (value === undefined) tx.objectStore('vault').delete(key);
+    else tx.objectStore('vault').put(value, key);
+    tx.oncomplete = () => resolve();
+    tx.onerror = tx.onabort = () => reject(tx.error);
+  });
+}
+export async function recipient(db) {
+  // Serialize initialization across tabs so existing notes never lose their recipient key.
+  const existing = await read(db, 'recipient');
+  if (existing) return existing;
+  const pair = createRecipient();
+  try {
+    const wrappingKey = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+    const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));
+    const encryptedSecret = await crypto.subtle.encrypt(
+      { name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: new TextEncoder().encode('daily-grind/recipient/v1') },
+      wrappingKey, pair.secretKey,
+    );
+    const candidate = { publicKey: pair.publicKey, wrappingKey, iv, encryptedSecret };
+    return await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+      const tx = db.transaction('vault', 'readwrite');
+      const store = tx.objectStore('vault');
+      const request = store.get('recipient');
+      let result;
+      request.onsuccess = () => {
+        result = request.result || candidate;
+        if (!request.result) store.put(candidate, 'recipient');
+      };
+      tx.oncomplete = () => resolve(result);
+      tx.onerror = tx.onabort = () => reject(tx.error);
+    });
+  } finally { pair.secretKey.fill(0); }
+}
+export async function unlockRecipient(record) {
+  return new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt(
+    { name: 'AES-GCM', iv: record.iv, additionalData: new TextEncoder().encode('daily-grind/recipient/v1') },
+    record.wrappingKey, record.encryptedSecret,
+  ));
+}

+# Script performance diagnostics
+
+Open the website with `?scriptDiagnostics=1` appended to its URL (or
+`&scriptDiagnostics=1` if it already has query parameters). Open the developer
+console and use the page normally to capture load and interaction work.
+
+In supported browsers, a console table automatically shows scripts accumulating
+more than 100 ms of execution inside slow animation frames. Results accumulate
+throughout the visit and are sorted by total execution time, so repeated small
+invocations can identify a heavy contributor too.
+
+- `scriptDiagnostics.report()` prints the top 20 sources, including those below
+  the automatic threshold, and returns the complete retained report.
+- `scriptDiagnostics.stop()` stops monitoring and returns a final report.
+- Reload without the query parameter to disable diagnostics. Reload with it to
+  begin a fresh measurement.
+
+The table includes total duration, invocation count, longest invocation duration,
+forced style/layout time, and the source location and invoker of the longest
+invocation. Source positions are character offsets, not line numbers. Start with
+the highest cumulative times and inspect those locations in developer tools.
+Forced style/layout time is part of script work; do not add it to total duration.
+
+This uses the Long Animation Frames API (frames exceeding 50 ms) with buffered
+observation to include earlier frames. It measures attributed script work within
+slow frames, **not** network loading, all JavaScript execution, or the exact
+blocking time attributable to a script. Browser attribution can omit short
+invocations, cross-origin frames, workers, or unavailable sources. Frames without
+script attribution are counted separately; an empty table does not prove the
+page is fast. Use current Chrome or Edge; unsupported browsers receive an
+informational console message and no observer is installed.
+
+Aggregates are capped at 200 source URLs, with omitted invocations counted in
+the report. No raw frame history is retained and no data is sent or saved.
+Source URLs can contain private query parameters: review reports before sharing.
+The current static page has no application or third-party scripts; the observer
+will help identify slow scripts when they are added or injected at runtime.
+
+The diagnostics script is deferred and exits immediately unless enabled. It adds
+one small same-origin request during normal visits. No dependencies or build
+step are required.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static HTML with INP diagnostics. Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
+Run `pnpm build` after upgrading `web-vitals` to refresh the checked-in, self-hosted
+attribution module, source map, and license in `vendor/`. No server is required to
+build. Deploy `index.html`, `inp-diagnostics.js`, and `vendor/` together.
+
+## Reading INP diagnostics
+
+`window.dailyGrindINP` contains the latest INP candidate report. Consumers can also
+listen for `window`'s `daily-grind:inp` custom event and read `event.detail`.
+Reports update when the INP candidate changes and when the library finalizes a
+changed metric on page hide. They are not a log of every interaction. Use the
+latest value per metric `id` in analytics, rather than counting each update as a
+separate page visit. The library handles outliers and back/forward cache restores.
+No interaction, or no Event Timing support, means no report, not a zero INP score.
+
+The three phase durations and `dominantPhase` indicate where to investigate:
+
+- `inputDelay`: work already blocking the main thread before handlers can run.
+- `processingDuration`: work during event processing, including synchronous layout.
+- `presentationDelay`: work between event processing and the next visible frame.
+
+`longestScript` identifies a script URL, function, character position, invoker,
+and the phase it overlaps most. This is supporting evidence, not proof of a sole
+cause. Rendering and forced style/layout timings distinguish CSS/style costs from
+geometry/layout costs when supported. Combined style/layout timings remain
+available on older implementations. Missing measurements are `null`, not zero;
+LoAF support and frame count distinguish unavailable data from no matching frame.
+Frame-level durations can extend outside the interaction and are not additive
+subparts of INP. Scripts shorter than 5 ms and frames shorter than 50 ms may not
+have attribution. Stable `data-inp-target` labels identify page controls without
+collecting text or input values; script URL queries and fragments are stripped.
+
+## Production collection
+
+This static app has no analytics backend. To collect field reports, configure an
+existing same-origin JSON POST collector by adding this to the document head:
+
+```html
+<meta name="inp-report-endpoint" content="/your-existing-collector">
+```
+
+The collector must be implemented separately and accept `application/json`.
+Configured reports use `sendBeacon`, with a keepalive `fetch` fallback when the
+beacon is unavailable or rejected. Delivery is best effort, with no retries or
+offline persistence. Without configuration, reports stay in memory and custom
+events only. No requests are sent to an assumed analytics endpoint.

+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+The homepage is a small static document with inline CSS, system fonts, and no client JavaScript. The largest concrete opportunity was its remote hero photograph. The optimized page serves the same photograph locally in responsive AVIF and WebP formats with a JPEG fallback, and exposes it directly to the HTML preload scanner. Mobile navigation and card sizing now accommodate narrow viewports.
+
+This is a source and asset audit of `index.html`, `package.json`, and the committed image files. No browser, development server, preview server, or server entrypoint was used. Actual LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB, visual rendering, and production cache behavior remain unmeasured; byte savings below are asset measurements, not timing predictions.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Priority | Area | Finding | Result |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| High | LCP discovery | The hero was a CSS background pointing to Unsplash, with no explicit fetch priority. | A static `picture` exposes the resource in HTML; the single hero `img` uses eager loading and high priority. |
+| High | LCP transfer | Every viewport referenced the same 1350px remote image. | Local 640, 960, 1350, and 1920px AVIF and WebP candidates use width descriptors and `sizes="100vw"`. Browsers select one supported candidate; JPEG is the fallback. |
+| Medium | Network dependencies | The critical image required a separate third-party connection. | Homepage rendering now needs only the site origin. Content hashes in asset filenames support safe immutable caching when configured on the host. |
+| Medium | Mobile interactions | Navigation could extend beyond the screen because its flex rows did not wrap. | Both rows wrap; navigation links have a 44px minimum height. Mobile navigation no longer remains sticky over the content. Keyboard focus is visible. |
+| Medium | Layout robustness | A 250px grid minimum could overflow very narrow containers. Fixed hero height could clip enlarged text. | The grid minimum is capped at available width. The hero has a minimum height, can expand for content, and uses small viewport units with a `vh` fallback. |
+| Maintain | CLS | The original background did not affect document flow; it already had reserved hero space. | The replacement image is absolutely positioned inside a reserved hero, with intrinsic dimensions. Image arrival cannot push the sections below it. No measured CLS reduction is claimed. |
+| Maintain | INP | There are no event handlers, polling timers, hydration, third-party scripts, or JavaScript bundles to optimize. | Navigation remains native links with no added client code. Reduced-motion preferences disable link transitions. No JavaScript long-task defect was found in the supplied code. |
+| Maintain | Critical path | Small inline CSS and system fonts already avoid stylesheet and font requests. | These are preserved. No additional preload, framework, service worker, or rendering-containment machinery was added to this small page. |
+
+Making the LCP candidate discoverable in HTML and assigning high fetch priority follows [web.dev responsive image guidance](https://web.dev/learn/design/responsive-images). Small viewport units use the small viewport size; the preceding `vh` declaration supports browsers that do not understand `svh`. See [MDN length units](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/length).
+
+## Measured asset sizes
+
+The original Unsplash URL returned 157,969 bytes during this audit. Its automatic format negotiation can produce different responses for different clients. Savings below compare the committed assets against that specific response.
+
+| Image candidate | AVIF bytes | WebP bytes | AVIF reduction versus original response |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| 640px | 13,381 | 16,900 | 91.5% |
+| 960px | 21,061 | 30,358 | 86.7% |
+| 1350px | 33,485 | 49,440 | 78.8% |
+| 1920px | 58,351 | 83,388 | 63.1% |
